text: Git branching helps developers work on different tasks without affecting the main code. A common practice is to create feature branches, where you build a new feature or fix a bug separately. Once your work is ready, you merge the branch back into the main branch. Before merging, teams often open a pull request so others can review the changes and discuss them. This creates a clear version control workflow: create a branch, make commits, open a pull request, review, and merge. Using branches keeps the project stable and makes teamwork easier.
